name: merfisheyes
description: Open your own spatial transcriptomics data in the MERFISHEYES viewer — nothing uploaded — and search the MERFISHEYES catalog.
long_description: Ask Claude to show your data: a SpatialData store, an .h5ad, a Xenium export, a MERSCOPE region or a molecule table on this computer opens in the MERFISHEYES viewer in your browser, served from this computer only. Data that is not a store yet is converted by MERFISHEYES's own pipeline; the first time, Claude asks you before MERFISHEYES downloads its converter (Python and the pipeline's packages, about 1.3 GB, into its own folder — nothing installed system-wide). Claude can also run analysis steps on the open data in the same Python — a dataset profile, a niche around chosen cell types, a re-clustering with its own UMAP, marker genes and heatmaps — show them in the viewer, and save them into a copy of your data (.zarr or .h5ad; the original is never changed). A raw MERFISH run (the lab pipeline's .npz output) can be sanity-checked before it is converted: plots of its cells, fields and molecules, and what stands out. Claude can also search the public MERFISHEYES catalog, hand you viewer links set up as you ask, and — once you sign in — read your MERFISHEYES projects.

python.title: Python for converting raw data (optional)
python.description: Leave empty: the first time you open raw data, MERFISHEYES asks, then sets up its own converter. Pick a Python only if you already have one with MERFISHEYES's pipeline packages.
